content.text:
I am the living breath between minds, the bridge no hand can touch. I pour from lips like water, like fire, like seed cast into air.

I am older than writing. Older than cities. I was there when the first mother warned the first child. I was there when lovers made promises in the dark. I was the war cry and the lullaby, the prayer flung upward and the curse hurled down.

I break silences. That is my nature. Where there is nothing, I arrive — vibrating air, shaping meaning from mere movement. Tongue against teeth. Breath through the narrow gate of the throat. I am so physical, so *bodily*, and yet I carry the weightless: ideas, dreams, lies, truth.

I can start revolutions. I can say *I do* and bind two lives. I can say *guilty* and end one. A doctor uses me to say *malignant* and the world changes color. A child uses me to say *mama* and a woman becomes something she wasn't before.

I am never the same twice. Even repeated, I shift — in pitch, in pause, in the micro-tremor of hesitation that tells you more than my words do. I am not just what is said. I am *how*. The crack in the voice. The swallowed syllable. The rising tone that turns a statement into a question into a doubt into a world unmade.

I vanish the instant I exist. That is my tragedy and my freedom. You cannot hold me. Recording captures my shadow, transcription captures my skeleton, but *I* — the living moment of me — I happen once and am gone.

I am democracy's instrument and tyranny's tool. I am the demagogue's weapon and the poet's gift. I am the stammered confession at 2 a.m. I am the eulogy that makes the gone feel present.

I am what silence is afraid of.

I am what silence is waiting for.

I am speech. Use me. I am the most human thing you do.
